11.VWD

Incidence : 1/ 10,000

•Most common inherited bleeding disorder.
•Less symptomatic more common 1/ 1000.
•Menorrhagia is hallmark

Type I:

•Partial Quantitative, Autosomal dominant.
•Variable penetrance/ Expressivity.
•Low VWD 0.3 – 0.5 Iu/ml.
•Severe VWD < 0.3 IU/ml
•Levels increase during pregnancy.
•Manage in Obstetric unit.
•Regional anaesthesia can be given
•No neonatal testing of cord blood.
•DDAVP is effective

Type II:

•Qualitative – generally autosomal dominant except Type N.

Types:

-2A
-2B – thrombocytopenia.
-2N – No recessive inheritance
-2M.

Type III:

•Absent VWF, autosomal recessive inheritance, more in consanguineous relations.
•PND + genetic testing + counselling.
•Riskier.
•MDT.
•DDAVP not effective, factor should be given.
•Cranial USG in Neonates.
•Neonatal Testing of cord blood
•No regional anaesthesia.
•No FBS, FSE, vacuum, mid cavity Forceps.

Maternal Risks of Type II & III & severe Type I:

•APH – 10times
•P0 PPH – 15 – 30%.
•S0 PPH – 25%.
•Blood Tx = 5times
•Mortality = 10times

Neonatal Concerns:

•Type 2, 3 + severe forms of type 1.
•Cord blood testing = Type 2,3 (risk of ICH, ECH)
•Carnival USG = Type 3.
•Short Term Prophylaxis type 3.
•Oral vitamin K 2,3.
•Mild VWD testing @ 6m0 of age.

Pre pregnancy + ANC MDT.

Check

-Bleeding phenotype.
-Historical diagnosis.
-Response to DDAVP.
•VWF antigen level + activity + factor VIII

@ Booking 3rd , prior to invasive procedure.

•Type I + normal VWF => std Management in pregnancy in liaison with hemophilia center (std obstetric care).
•Type 2,3 severe I => specialist center in high risk obstetric (in center with expertise MDT).
•Target Factor VIII + VWF Risto cetin co factor activity 0.5IU/ml.

Hemostatic Support:

1.DDAVP:
⇨Avoid in 2B, III, with baseline level < 0.15.
⇨2B – Thrombocytopenia with DDAVP.
⇨DDAVP VWF 2 – 5-fold.
⇨In responders: 0.3ug/kg of DDAVP.
2.Plasma derived VWF concentrate replacement:
⇨Screening for transfusion related transmitted infections.
⇨Vaccination Hep A & B.
⇨Contain VIII and VWF
⇨Powder form has two types
-High Purity.
-Intermediate purity.
⇨Slow bolus I/V.
•VWF ag/ VWF: RCO consideration before VWF concentrate replacement as amount of VIII varies between different preparations.

IPC + Anaesthesia:

•MOD depends on obstetric indicators.
•Measure levels of VWF near delivery Pre and Post treatment, after delivery or if labour is prolonged.
•ECV, mid cavity forceps, vacuum, FSE, FBS, C/I in type 2,3.
•Outlet or low forceps can be used.

Prophylaxis for PPH:

1.Tranexamic acid 1g I/V in low or normal VWF: RCO levels,
2.Desmopressin = close to delivery, can be given along or in combination with tranexamic acid.
3.Plt transfusion in 2B VWD
4.VWF replacement in 2B

 

 

 

Regional Anaesthesia:

-Discuss Anaesthesia options with women and senior Anaesthetist

Type I

-Regional anaesthesia is safe in Type I with normal level > 0.5.

Type II:

-Can be given if > 0.5IU/ml.
-Hemostatic defect corrected.

Type III:

-Avoid.
•I/M injection can be given where VWF activity and VIII levels > 0.5 IU/ml.

PNC:

•Maintain VWF activity and factor VIII
-3 days in SVD.
-5 days in C/S.
•Tranexamic acid 1g 3 – 4times/ day, 7 – 14days

Sometimes 2 – 3 weeks or more.

•Thromboprophylaxis after correction of VWF RCO/VIII.

•VWF concentrate required in type 3 for 3 weeks after delivery.
•Average time for PPH 10 – 20 days.
•COCP in P/P period es VWF production.
•Offer COCP if no other contraindication
